text:
ReleaseBot: starting rolling deploy: service=inference-runtime env=prod pipeline=release-2026-03-15-canary
ReleaseBot: pushed tag=canary-20260315-ffed digest=sha256:beefdead1234
Anya: paging oncall, huge 5xx spike on inference-runtime - dashboards green -> red in last 8m :rotating_light:
Anya: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/inference-runtime?from=now-10m
Kelly: customers reporting /v1/generate timeouts and some 502s in EU region
IncidentBot: Incident created INC-2026-03-15-ALPHA severity=P2 assignee=Dhruv
Dhruv: taking it. pulling pod logs now
Dhruv: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-runtime-canary -o wide — several CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled
Samir: logs show repeated checksum failure during KV restore: "kv_cache: checksum mismatch - header=0x4b7a got=0xdeadbeef" and then memory alloc failures
Samir: tail: ```2026-03-15T10:14:02Z ERROR kv_cache: checksum mismatch header=0x4b7a got=0xdeadbeef
2026-03-15T10:14:05Z WARN model: partial weights mapped, falling back to streamed init
2026-03-15T10:14:09Z ERROR memory: failed to allocate 1.8GB```
Anya: that smells like a bad image/artifact - maybe build cache reused a wrong layer or registry tag was annotated incorrectly
Dhruv: checking registry digest vs claim from pipeline
Dhruv: gcloud container images describe gcr.redwood-inference/internal/inference-runtime:canary-20260315-ffed --format='get(image_summary.fully_qualified_digest)' -> sha256:beefcafe9999 (does NOT match ReleaseBot digest)
ReleaseBot: pipeline log excerpt: "[push] uploaded digest=sha256:beefdead1234 tag=canary-20260315-ffed" then "[compose] base layer digest=sha256:beefcafe9999" then "[push] tagged canary-20260315-ffed -> sha256:beefcafe9999 (warning: tag bound to different digest than upload)"
Kelly: so the pipeline reported one digest but the tag actually points to another blob in the registry - potential cache poisoning or build-layer race during concurrent uploads
Samir: customer impact: estimated 150 failed requests over last 12 minutes across 5 orgs, some retried, some billed. Need a quick mitigation to stop canary traffic and rollback
Dhruv: mitigation plan: 1) flip kill-switch runtime.enable_canary=false 2) scale down canary deployment 3) roll inference-runtime to last-known-good stable image 4) pause pipeline and add temporary block on tag pushes
Dhruv: toggling feature flag runtime.enable_canary -> false (console)
Operator: feature flag runtime.enable_canary set to false by Dhruv at 2026-03-15T10:17Z
Anya: seeing reduction in new canary traffic, but pods still failing from existing canary replicas
Dhruv: kubectl -n prod scale deployment/inference-runtime-canary --replicas=0
Dhruv: scaling... pods terminating
Samir: starting rollback to stable: stable-20260310-9f2
Dhruv: kubectl -n prod set image deployment/inference-runtime inference-runtime=gcr.redwood-inference/internal/inference-runtime:stable-20260310-9f2
Dhruv: rollout status: "deployment \"inference-runtime\" successfully rolled out"
Anya: error rate trending back to baseline, latency normalizing :thumbsup:
Kelly: customer ops: notified affected customers, CS engaged for billing/help tickets
CI-Team: halting release pipeline release-2026-03-15-canary and investigating cache behaviour
CI-Team: pipeline canceled manually and automatic gating engaged
Samir: registry audit shows suspicious sequence: ```2026-03-15T10:12:44 upload blob sha256:beefdead1234 by ci-runner-12
2026-03-15T10:12:58 upload complete
2026-03-15T10:13:02 another blob sha256:beefcafe9999 uploaded
2026-03-15T10:13:05 tag push canary-20260315-ffed -> sha256:beefcafe9999
2026-03-15T10:13:08 tag annotated with metadata referencing earlier upload digest```
Dhruv: looks like a race where two different builds uploaded different blobs and the tag ended up pointing to the wrong blob; enforce registry immutability and tag -> digest verification in CI
Dhruv: blocking new tag pushes until CI adds digest-verify step
Dhruv: creating postmortem ticket PM-2026-0315-REGISTRY and assigning CI and registry teams
Anya: I'm handing off — I need to step out in 25m. Dhruv, you own the incident and postmortem, please follow up on customer comms
Dhruv: acknowledged, taking over. I'll collect full log bundles and link to ticket
Samir: adding log-based alert: "kv_cache checksum mismatch" -> Sev2 so we catch this earlier
Operator: Incident INC-2026-03-15-ALPHA updated: mitigations applied (canary disabled, rollback complete), customers notified
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-03-15-ALPHA status=mitigated closed_by=Dhruv closed_at=2026-03-15T10:42:00 note="postmortem assigned"
Dhruv: action items: (A) CI: add digest verification in push step, (B) Registry: enforce immutability & reject tag pushes that don't match declared digest, (C) Runtime: add startup alert for KV checksum mismatch, (D) Postmortem in 48h with impact numbers
Kelly: regional note: EU traffic routed to canary nodes first which increased visibility there; check routing rules for canary affinity
Anya: thanks team for fast coordination. I'll loop back with CS on any escalations later
CI-Team: we found the root cause in cache reuse on shared build-hosts - patching cache key derivation now
Dhruv: I'll keep the ticket updated and confirm fixes in next deployment window
Operator: Incident INC-2026-03-15-ALPHA closed as mitigated at 2026-03-15T10:42Z
